answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the network maps agents across a trust graph where identity clusters harbor audited stakes. Game-theoretic multi-agent auditing enforces topological cut verifications across graph bottlenecks: to validate fraudulent identities across an ocean of synthetic peers, an attacker must cross bottlenecks and reach a high-trust consensus summit. Failing audits triggers stake slashing, imposing superlinear attacker cost scaling with cut capacity.
